observations: Full UI inventory, upload/rename/download/delete lifecycle, and data-source confirmation completed with before/after evidence and network capture for every mutating action.

Several individual findings are single-sample (e.g. duplicate-name upload allowed, invalid-format client block) and are explicitly marked knowledge_kind OBSERVED_CURRENT with LOW per-finding confidence in unknowns — do not generalize as confirmed business rules from one sample.

Pre-existing store state already contained 3 custom fonts (ids 915/916/917) with 'ago' timestamps of 12-13h, including one named 'QA Renamed Baginda' that strongly suggests a prior QA rename test on this same store/date — documented as initial_state, not created by this run, and left untouched (no delete/rename beyond what this run itself created).
unknowns: ACT-02-02-001 first upload attempt (network index 45) failed with net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR at transport level (no HTTP response). Treated as environment/network noise, not evidence of any duplicate-name business rule. Retried immediately and the retry (index 46) succeeded with 201, which IS used as evidence.

ACT-02-03-001 (invalid format upload) produced no literal error text in the DOM, only a warning-triangle icon (la-exclamation-triangle) with no title/aria-label — recorded verbatim; the exact user-facing meaning of that icon (vs. a text tooltip that might exist but wasn't triggered) is unknown.

Duplicate-name upload allowed (no uniqueness validation observed) is based on a single sample (ACT-02-02-001) — confidence LOW for this specific finding, do not treat as a confirmed platform-wide rule.

Download filename discrepancy: server content-disposition header names a UUID (1df707cc-....ttf), Playwright's download event reports 'Hey Magnolia.ttf' (original upload filename), and the card's current display name at download time was 'QA CTX-20260910-05 Hey Magnolia'. The exact client-side logic that produced 'Hey Magnolia.ttf' as the saved filename is not confirmed from network evidence alone (likely cached original filename in front-end component state) — flagged as unknown, not asserted as a bug or a confirmed rule.

Whether Show entries / search / page-size selections persist across a real page reload was not tested (store only had ≤5 fonts total, so multi-page pagination behavior and the old KB's 'URL doesn't change, refresh returns to page 1' claim could not be re-verified on this store).

observations.observed_result: DIFFERS from old KB (different store, 2026-09-09): on THIS store it opens a MODAL dialog ('Browse fonts to upload:' heading, warning banner 'Convert font into TTF before uploading (Online converter)' linking to transfonter.org, and a 'Choose File' button), not a direct-to-OS-picker with no modal. 'Choose File' then opens the native OS file chooser. Input DOM: <input type="file" id="new-font" multiple accept=".otf,.ttf">. Selecting a file auto-uploads (no separate submit button found) and the filename appears under a 'New fonts' list with a status icon.

Selecting 'Fallback to a custom font' reveals 'Fallback Font' field with 'No font selected' + 'Select a font' button (differs from old KB's store which had a font already configured there — expected data difference, not a conflict). Selecting the radio fires 0 network requests (client-side only state until Save, which was NOT clicked in this run).

Verbatim: heading 'Confirm'; body 'Are you sure to remove Hey Magnolia?' followed by bullets '- This action could make design corrupted if you already use it in artwork or font category' and '- If you want to replace a font, you can rename old one and upload new one'; buttons 'Remove' / 'Cancel'.

observations.element: Canvas toolbar Font family selector on a selected text ('Paragraph') layer: 'Font type' radios 'Google Fonts' / 'Custom Fonts', and when Custom Fonts is chosen, a 'Select a font' button opening 'Your Custom Fonts' — the SAME picker component/data as the standalone /fonts page (same GraphQL getData/custom_fonts_connection query, same card layout, plus a 'Select' action per card).
observations.observed_result: Fonts uploaded via /fonts (this run's 'QA CTX-20260910-05 Hey Magnolia', id 920, plus the 3 pre-existing fonts) all appear in this picker. Confirms custom fonts are directly usable as a text layer's font without going through a separate Font Category step.
